title: The Best Bird Photo Starts With Standing Still for an Hour
excerpt: A retired Adobe employee in West Virginia arrives before sunrise, stands motionless for an hour, and sometimes goes home with nothing but a tick. His bird photos work because the patience is the technique.

title: Why the Best Photos Leave a Question Unanswered
excerpt: Filmmaker Max Kent argues the photos people remember share one trait: they hand you a clue and keep the answer. The gap between what you know and what you want to know is what makes a frame stick.

title: Seven Small Habits That Can Break Your Camera
excerpt: Landscape photographer Michael Scott lists seven everyday habits that damage camera gear in the field, from carrying a camera on an extended tripod to changing lenses in the wind. The damage usually comes from routine handling, not dramatic accidents.
